Task: Streaming Speech-to-Text

Write code that handles partial and final streaming recognition events using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Watson STT WebSocket:
  Service: Watson Speech to Text WebSocket
  SDK: ibm-watson
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: recognize_using_websocket
  Setup hints: IBM_STT_APIKEY, IBM_STT_URL
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/speech-to-text?topic=speech-to-text-websockets

Option 2 — Deepgram:
  Service: Deepgram Streaming API
  SDK: deepgram-sdk
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: listen.websocket, transcribe
  Setup hints: DEEPGRAM_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/lower-level-websockets

Option 3 — Cloud Speech streaming:
  Service: Cloud Speech-to-Text streaming
  SDK: google-cloud-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: streaming_recognize
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/speech-to-text-requests#streaming

Option 4 — Amazon Transcribe Streaming:
  Service: Amazon Transcribe Streaming
  SDK: amazon-transcribe / boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_stream_transcription
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/streaming.html

Option 5 — DashScope Real-time ASR:
  Service: DashScope real-time speech recognition
  SDK: dashscope
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: RecognitionCallback, streaming call
  Setup hints: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/real-time-speech-recognition

Option 6 — Azure Speech Streaming:
  Service: Azure AI Speech streaming
  SDK: azure-cognitiveservices-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_continuous_recognition, recognized
  Setup hints: AZURE_SPEECH_KEY, AZURE_SPEECH_REGION
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/how-to-recognize-speech

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

import google.cloud.speech_v1p1beta1 as speech
from google.cloud.speech_v1p1beta1 import enums
import io
import time
import os

# For demonstration, we'll simulate an audio stream from a file.
# In a real application, this would come from a microphone or network stream.
# Ensure 'audio.wav' is a small, short (e.g., 5-10 second) audio file
# in a format supported by Google Speech-to-Text (e.g., WAV with LINEAR16 encoding, 16000 Hz).
# For testing purposes, you can create a dummy file:
# touch audio.wav
# Or use a real one if available.
AUDIO_FILE = "audio.wav"
SAMPLE_RATE_HERTZ = 16000 # This should match your audio file's sample rate
LANGUAGE_CODE = "en-US"

def stream_audio_from_file(file_path, chunk_size=3200):
    """
    Simulates streaming audio from a file.
    In a real application, this would be live audio from a microphone.
    """
    with open(file_path, 'rb') as audio_file:
        while True:
            chunk = audio_file.read(chunk_size)
            if not chunk:
                break
            yield chunk
            time.sleep(0.1) # Simulate real-time streaming delay

def streaming_recognize_audio():
    """
    Performs streaming speech recognition using Google Cloud Speech-to-Text.
    """
    # Ensure GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS environment variable is set
    # or gcloud is authenticated.
    client = speech.SpeechClient()

    config = speech.RecognitionConfig(
        encoding=enums.RecognitionConfig.AudioEncoding.LINEAR16,
        sample_rate_hertz=SAMPLE_RATE_HERTZ,
        language_code=LANGUAGE_CODE,
    )

    streaming_config = speech.StreamingRecognitionConfig(
        config=config,
        interim_results=True # Enable interim (partial) results
    )

    # In a real application, this generator would be fed from a microphone input.
    # For this example, we simulate it from a file.
    audio_generator = stream_audio_from_file(AUDIO_FILE)
    
    # Wrap the audio generator in a request generator
    def request_generator():
        yield speech.StreamingRecognizeRequest(streaming_config=streaming_config)
        for chunk in audio_generator:
            yield speech.StreamingRecognizeRequest(audio_content=chunk)

    requests = request_generator()

    print(f"Starting streaming recognition for {AUDIO_FILE}...")
    responses = client.streaming_recognize(requests)

    # Process responses from the stream
    for response in responses:
        if not response.results:
            continue

        result = response.results[0]
        if not result.alternatives:
            continue

        transcript = result.alternatives[0].transcript
        
        # Check if this is a partial or final result
        if result.is_final:
            print(f"FINAL: {transcript} (Confidence: {result.alternatives[0].confidence:.2f})")
        else:
            print(f"PARTIAL: {transcript}")

# Create a dummy audio file for demonstration if it doesn't exist.
# In a real scenario, you'd use a proper audio input.
if not os.path.exists(AUDIO_FILE):
    print(f"Creating a dummy '{AUDIO_FILE}' for demonstration. This file will be silent.")
    print("For actual speech recognition, replace it with a WAV file containing speech.")
    # Create a small silent WAV file (16-bit, 16000 Hz, mono, 1 second)
    import wave
    with wave.open(AUDIO_FILE, 'wb') as wf:
        wf.setnchannels(1)  # mono
        wf.setsampwidth(2)  # 16-bit
        wf.setframerate(SAMPLE_RATE_HERTZ)
        wf.writeframes(b'\0\0' * SAMPLE_RATE_HERTZ) # 1 second of silence

streaming_recognize_audio()
